metadata.title: TSMC Rises Ahead of Nvidia's Critical AI Demand Test

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE:TSM), the world's largest contract chipmaker, jumped approximately 0.9% to $419.40 Friday morning as investors locked onto Nvidia's August 26 earnings. This is not just another quarterly report. Nvidia's (NASDAQ:NVDA) guidance will reveal whether demand for advanced chips, premium packaging and AI accelerators is still racing aheador finally catching its breath.
TSMC is betting billions that the AI machine keeps roaring. July revenue exploded 44.7% to NT$467.58 billion, while management raised its 2026 capital-spending forecast to between $60 billion and $64 billion. Some market estimates push 2027 spending as high as $85 billion. Nvidia, Apple, AMD, Broadcom and hyperscaler-designed chips all need TSMC's leading-edge factories. The demand pipeline looks huge. So does the bill.
The stock's valuation says Wall Street expects near-perfect execution. TSMC has climbed roughly 38% this year and trades near 30 times earnings. At $419.40, the shares also stand 31.3% above their $319.43 GF Value estimatea clear sign that investors are paying aggressively for the AI future. Nvidia's outlook could validate that premium. A weaker signal could hit fast, because TSMC is no longer priced like an overlooked foundry. It is priced like the factory behind the entire AI boom.
